[Help](https://help.shopify.com/en) [Log in](https://help.shopify.com/en/user/login?returnTo=%2Fen%2Fmanual%2Fshopify-admin%2Fproductivity-tools%2Fbulk-actions) Contents [Home](https://help.shopify.com/en) [Shopify admin](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-admin) [Productivity tools](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-admin/productivity-tools) # Using bulk actions in your Shopify admin You can perform actions in bulk in the Shopify admin, such as fulfilling many orders, deleting many files, or publishing many products in one action. Bulk actions can save time by letting you complete repetitive tasks across multiple items at once. You can use bulk actions on many pages of your Shopify admin, including [**Orders**](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/fulfillment/managing-orders), [**Products**](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products), [**Customers**](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/customers), and [**Discounts**](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/discounts). The more information you try to bulk change at one time, the longer your bulk changes will take to complete. You can also use a CSV file to bulk edit a larger number of list items for your [products](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/import-export), your [inventory](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/inventory/setup/inventory-csv), or your [customers](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/customers/import-export-customers). After your CSV file is uploaded in your Shopify admin, you receive a confirmation email from Shopify at the email account that you used to set up your Shopify store. ## On this page - [Select items to edit in bulk](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-admin/productivity-tools/bulk-actions#select-items-to-edit-in-bulk) - [Choose a bulk action](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-admin/productivity-tools/bulk-actions#choose-a-bulk-action-to-perform) - [Examples of bulk actions in your Shopify admin](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-admin/productivity-tools/bulk-actions#examples-of-bulk-action) - [Resources without 'Bulk edit' bulk action](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-admin/productivity-tools/bulk-actions#resources-without-bulk-edit-bulk-action) ## Select items to edit in bulk You can select items to perform bulk actions on many pages in your Shopify admin, including **Orders**, **Customers**, and **Products**. Some pages, such as **Discounts**, support bulk actions when using a desktop device, but not when using a mobile device. #### Steps: Desktop 1. From your Shopify admin, go to any page with a table of resources, such as **Orders** or **Customers**. 2. Do one of the following, depending on which options are available for the resource type: - To select items one by one, click the checkbox for each item that you want to select. - To select a range of items, click to select an item, and then hold the `Shift` key and click another item. This selects the first and last items that you clicked, and all items in between. - To select all items on a page, click the checkbox at the top of the item list. - To select all items from your store, click the checkbox at the top of the item list, and then click **Select all 50+ items**. - To select all items from a filtered view that contains more than 50 items, do any of the following steps: - Click the checkbox at the top of the item list, and then in the **50 selected** dropdown, click **Select all results**. This selects all items that match your current filter criteria. - Click the checkbox at the top of the item list, and then navigate to the next page in the view and click the checkbox at the top of the item list again. Repeat this step until you've selected as many items as required. Mobile 1. In the [Shopify app](https://www.shopify.com/install/detect), do one of the following: - From the [Shopify app](https://www.shopify.com/install/detect), tap the ![Orders](https://cdn.shopify.com/shopifycloud/help-center/manual/admin-icons/OrderIcon.svg) icon . Tap the **⋮** menu, and then tap **Select orders**. - From the [Shopify app](https://www.shopify.com/install/detect), tap the ![Products](https://cdn.shopify.com/shopifycloud/help-center/manual/admin-icons/ProductIcon.svg) icon . Tap the **⋮** menu, and then tap **Select products**. - Tap the ![Menu](https://cdn.shopify.com/shopifycloud/help-center/manual/admin-icons/MenuIcon.svg) icon, and then tap **Customers**. Tap the **⋮** menu, and then tap **Select customers**. 2. Tap the checkbox next to each item that you want to select. You can select up to 25 items at a time on a mobile device. ## Choose a bulk action Bulk actions are the actions that you can perform for multiple resources at one time. The available bulk actions vary depending on the type of resource that you're performing the bulk action on. For example, the bulk action options for your **Customers** list include bulk editing, merging customers, adding or removing tags, adding to a company, deleting customers, or [running a Shopify Flow automation manually](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-flow/manage/manual#run-a-workflow-manually-with-a-bulk-action). However, the bulk action options for your customer **Segments** list is limited to deleting segments in bulk. Common bulk actions display at the top of the selected items list as separate buttons. Any other bulk actions are contained in the ![More actions](https://cdn.shopify.com/shopifycloud/help-center/manual/admin-icons/MenuHorizontalIcon.svg) menu, including bulk actions offered by apps. Some bulk actions are available on both desktop and mobile devices, and some bulk actions are available on desktop devices only. #### Steps: Desktop 1. [Select the list items](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-admin/productivity-tools/bulk-actions#select-items-to-edit-in-bulk) that you want to perform a bulk action on. 2. Select the bulk action in one of the following ways: - Click the name of the bulk action, and then take the necessary steps for completing the action. - Click ![More actions](https://cdn.shopify.com/shopifycloud/help-center/manual/admin-icons/MenuHorizontalIcon.svg), then click the name of the bulk action, and then take the necessary steps for completing the action. 3. Optional: If you're deleting list items, then confirm your choice by clicking **Delete**. Mobile 1. [Select the list items](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-admin/productivity-tools/bulk-actions#select-items-to-edit-in-bulk) that you want to perform a bulk action on. 2. Select the bulk action in one of the following ways: - Tap the name of the bulk action, and then take the necessary steps for completing the action. - Tap **⋮**, then tap the name of the bulk action, and then take the necessary steps for completing the action. 3. Optional: If you're deleting list items, then confirm your choice by tapping **Delete**. ## Examples of bulk actions in your Shopify admin **Bulk actions** can be used on any of the following example pages of your Shopify admin, and each page has its own set of available actions. Bulk actions aren't limited to the pages or actions described in this list, as most resource tables in your Shopify admin can support bulk actions. Our app creates a _parent bundle product_ that must have **“Track quantity”: false** to function properly. This product is owned and managed by our app via productConfigurationOwner. Our understanding is **only the configuration owner should be able to update settings like track\_quantity** . However, we’ve found that: > Merchants (or other apps) can bypass this restriction using the Shopify bulk editor in the admin. This is causing the track\_quantity field to be unintentionally enabled, which results in our bundles appearing sold out, even when the components are in stock. We are now detecting and auto-correcting this state in our app, but the fact that it can be overridden in the admin UI contradicts the intended behavior of configuration ownership and creates support friction with merchants who didn’t knowingly change anything. ### [Heading link](https://community.shopify.dev/t/bulk-editor-allows-changes-to-track-quantity-on-app-owned-products-breaking-app-functionality/18108\#p-38558-steps-to-reproduce-1)**Steps to Reproduce:** 1. Create a product using an app with productConfigurationOwner set and track\_quantity = false. 2. Go to Shopify admin → Products → Bulk editor. 3. Select the bundle product. 4. Enable “Track quantity”. 5. Save changes. 6. The product is now incorrectly set to track\_quantity: true despite being owned by the app. * * * ### [Heading link](https://community.shopify.dev/t/bulk-editor-allows-changes-to-track-quantity-on-app-owned-products-breaking-app-functionality/18108\#p-38558-expected-behavior-2)**Expected Behavior:** Shopify should **block updates to configuration-managed fields like track\_quantity** if the user or app is not the productConfigurationOwner. # Products

The **Products** section in your Shopify admin helps you manage your store's entire product catalog, from basic product setup to advanced customization. There are also automation, AI, and bulk management tools that can help you save time when working on your business's product offerings.

### Features of the Products section

At minimum, a product in Shopify needs to have only two things: A title and a price. From there, you can add descriptions, images, videos, compare-at prices, inventory levels, variants, tags, metafields, and many other details that help you display and sell your products.

### Product details

When you add a product to Shopify, you can configure all the relevant settings for your product:

- Title and description: Craft SEO-friendly product names and descriptions using rich text formatting. Avoid duplicate manufacturer descriptions for better search visibility.
- Media: Upload images, 3D models, or videos to demonstrate products. Supports desktop and mobile layout adjustments and zoom functionality.
- Pricing and inventory: Set base prices, track stock quantities, and manage variant-specific inventory.

For a complete list of details and step-by-step instructions, refer to the [product details documentation](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/details/product-details-page).

### Product management

After you add your products, you can manage them individually or through bulk actions. You can organize them into collections to help apply certain settings to groups of products or display them together on your online store.

Review the following product management actions for more details and instructions:

- [Adding and updating products](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/add-update-products)
- [Organizing products into collections](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/collections)
- [Creating metafields for customized product details](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/custom-data/metafields)
- [Using product tags to group products](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-flow/reference/actions/add-product-tags)

You can also apply certain changes to many products at the same time, such as adjusting prices or changing sales channel visibility using the [bulk editor](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-admin/productivity-tools/bulk-editing). You can also make changes to your product catalog using [CSV files](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/import-export/using-csv).

### Connections to other Shopify admin sections

When your product catalog is set up, there are other areas in your Shopify admin that can reference these products to help set up the rest of your store:

- [Inventory and variants](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/inventory/setup): Manage stock levels per variant combination (size and color).
- [Online store menus](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/online-store/menus-and-links/editing-menus): Use collections to power store menus.
- [Shipping settings](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/fulfillment/setup): Create product-based rules for your shipping rates, such as basing them off of product price or weight.

### Sourcing products for your Shopify store

To source products from other businesses and sell them on your store, consider the following options:

- [Shopify Product Network](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/promoting-marketing/shopify-product-network): Recommended products from other Shopify stores appear on your store automatically. Recommendations are optimized based on customer data and your existing catalog. You earn commission when customers buy, and seller stores fulfill their own line items. You don't import these products into your catalog or stock them yourself.
- [Shopify Collective](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/online-sales-channels/shopify-collective/retailers): You choose suppliers and import specific brands and products into your catalog, and earn a margin on each sale with no upfront inventory costs. You curate what you want to sell.
- [Dropshipping apps](https://apps.shopify.com/categories/finding-products-sourcing-options-dropshipping): Find third-party suppliers in the Shopify App Store who fulfill orders directly to your customers.
- [Print-on-demand apps](https://apps.shopify.com/categories/finding-products-sourcing-options-print-on-demand-pod): Sell custom printed products that are printed and shipped by the app provider.

If you’re using DecoNetwork (DN) to manage your fulfillment, it’s essential to properly configure your products in Shopify to be fulfilled in DN. This setup ensures that your inventory management is seamless and your products are processed efficiently, helping you save time and reduce manual errors. In this guide, we’ll walk you through the steps to update multiple products at once, enabling them to be fulfilled in DN.

## To bulk-edit Shopify inventory for fulfillment in DecoNetwork:

01. Open your web browser and go to your Shopify Admin page.
02. Enter your login credentials and click **Log in**.
03. From your Shopify Admin dashboard, navigate to **Products** in the left-hand menu.

    [![Select Product.png](https://help.deconetwork.com/hc/article_attachments/29151602236571)](https://help.deconetwork.com/hc/en-us/articles/29151581505563-Bulk-editing-Shopify-Inventory-for-Fulfillment-in-DecoNetwork#select-product)

    [![Select Product.png](https://help.deconetwork.com/hc/article_attachments/29151602236571)](https://help.deconetwork.com/hc/en-us/articles/29151581505563-Bulk-editing-Shopify-Inventory-for-Fulfillment-in-DecoNetwork#_)



    Click the image to enlarge.

04. Click on **Inventory** to open the inventory editor.

    [![Inventory Page.png](https://help.deconetwork.com/hc/article_attachments/29151618998299)](https://help.deconetwork.com/hc/en-us/articles/29151581505563-Bulk-editing-Shopify-Inventory-for-Fulfillment-in-DecoNetwork#inventory-page)

    [![Inventory Page.png](https://help.deconetwork.com/hc/article_attachments/29151618998299)](https://help.deconetwork.com/hc/en-us/articles/29151581505563-Bulk-editing-Shopify-Inventory-for-Fulfillment-in-DecoNetwork#_)



    Click the image to enlarge.

05. Select the DN shop location from the **Inventory** dropdown list. This is crucial if you manage stock across multiple locations.

    ![Inventory Location.png](https://help.deconetwork.com/hc/article_attachments/29151618998683)

06. Select the products you want to edit in bulk.
07. Click on the **Bulk edit** button.

    ![Bulk Edit Button.png](https://help.deconetwork.com/hc/article_attachments/29178406714139)

    The Bulk Edit screen is displayed.

    [![Bulk Edit Screen.png](https://help.deconetwork.com/hc/article_attachments/29178362853275)](https://help.deconetwork.com/hc/en-us/articles/29151581505563-Bulk-editing-Shopify-Inventory-for-Fulfillment-in-DecoNetwork#bulk-edit-screen)

    [![Bulk Edit Screen.png](https://help.deconetwork.com/hc/article_attachments/29178362853275)](https://help.deconetwork.com/hc/en-us/articles/29151581505563-Bulk-editing-Shopify-Inventory-for-Fulfillment-in-DecoNetwork#_)



    Click the image to enlarge.

08. For each SKU, double-click in the cell of the DN store location's _Available_ column or _On hand_ column.

    Make sure the **Stock at this location** checkbox is ticked.

    [![Stock at this Location Checkbox.png](https://help.deconetwork.com/hc/article_attachments/29179797063323)](https://help.deconetwork.com/hc/en-us/articles/29151581505563-Bulk-editing-Shopify-Inventory-for-Fulfillment-in-DecoNetwork#stock-at-checkbox)

    [![Stock at this Location Checkbox.png](https://help.deconetwork.com/hc/article_attachments/29179797063323)](https://help.deconetwork.com/hc/en-us/articles/29151581505563-Bulk-editing-Shopify-Inventory-for-Fulfillment-in-DecoNetwork#_)



    Click the image to enlarge.

09. Click **Save** to update the settings.

    ![Save Button.png](https://help.deconetwork.com/hc/article_attachments/29179844704155)

10. Click **Back**.

[Shopify admin](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-admin)

# Bulk editing
From your Shopify admin, you can select the products that you want to change, choose which properties you want to update, and then make your changes.

## Select list items to edit
You can select list items to edit in bulk in your Shopify admin.

#### Steps:
1. From your Shopify admin, click [**Products**](https://admin.shopify.com/products), [**Collections**](https://admin.shopify.com/collections), [**Inventory**](https://admin.shopify.com/products/inventory), or [**Customers**](https://admin.shopify.com/customers).
web.markdown:
[Help](https://help.shopify.com/en)

[Log in](https://help.shopify.com/en/user/login?returnTo=%2Fen%2Fmanual%2Fshopify-admin%2Fproductivity-tools%2Fbulk-editing)

Contents

[Home](https://help.shopify.com/en)

[Shopify admin](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-admin)

[Productivity tools](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-admin/productivity-tools)

# Bulk editing

You can use the bulk editor tool to make changes to multiple products and product variants at the same time. From your Shopify admin, you can select the products that you want to change, choose which properties you want to update, and then make your changes.

When a product has multiple variants, then you can only bulk edit the inventory of the product from the [**Inventory**](https://admin.shopify.com/products/inventory) section in your Shopify admin.

You can also use the bulk editor to edit the properties of your collections and customers.

The more information you try to bulk change at one time, the longer your bulk changes will take to complete. You can also use a CSV file to bulk edit a larger number of list items for your [products](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/import-export), your [inventory](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/inventory/setup/inventory-csv), or your [customers](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/customers/import-export-customers). After your CSV file is uploaded in your Shopify admin, you receive a confirmation email from Shopify at the email account that you used to set up your Shopify store.

If you use the Microsoft Edge web browser to edit list items in bulk, then it can cause errors due to a limited URL length. Consider using other web browsers such as Chrome, Firefox, or Safari.

## On this page

- [Select list items to edit](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-admin/productivity-tools/bulk-editing#select-bulk)
- [Select list item properties to edit](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-admin/productivity-tools/bulk-editing#manage-properties)
- [Edit list item properties in bulk](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-admin/productivity-tools/bulk-editing#edit-list-item-properties-in-bulk)
- [Shortcuts in the bulk editor](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-admin/productivity-tools/bulk-editing#bulk-editor-shortcuts)
- [Update the invalid values, then save again error message](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-admin/productivity-tools/bulk-editing#update-the-invalid-values-then-save-again-error-message)
- [Variants aren't grouped together in inventory bulk editor](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-admin/productivity-tools/bulk-editing#variants-aren-t-grouped-together-in-inventory-bulk-editor)

## Select list items to edit

You can select list items to edit in bulk in your Shopify admin.

#### Steps:

1. From your Shopify admin, click [**Products**](https://admin.shopify.com/products), [**Collections**](https://admin.shopify.com/collections), [**Inventory**](https://admin.shopify.com/products/inventory), or [**Customers**](https://admin.shopify.com/customers).
2. Use the checkboxes to select each list item that you want to edit.
3. Click **Bulk edit**.

## Select list item properties to edit

The bulk editor displays the list items that you selected and some of their properties in a table. You can change which properties display in the table.

For example, if you're bulk editing your products, then each column in the table represents a product property, such as price, SKU, and compare-at price. Each row in the table represents a selected product or product variant.

To add a property to the bulk editing table, click **Columns**, and then select all the properties that you want to add to the table.

To remove a property from the bulk editing table, click **Columns**, and then deselect all the properties that you want to remove from the table.

## Edit list item properties in bulk

After you select the properties that you want to edit, you can click the fields in the table to enter new data or edit existing data.

#### Steps:

1. Click and then type in a field in the table to enter or edit the property for that list item.
2. Click **Save**. If any errors occur, then you need to fix them, and then click **Save** again.

## Shortcuts in the bulk editor

To help you navigate and edit list item properties efficiently in the bulk editor, you can use the following shortcuts. When multiple cells are selected, apply any edits to the outlined active cell to update all selected cells.

| Action | Shortcut |
| --- | --- |
| Move between cells | Click to select a table cell, and then press an arrow key on your keyboard to move to the next editable cell in that direction. |
| Select multiple cells that aren't adjacent | Hold the `Alt` key on a PC or the `command` key on a Mac and click different cells. |
| Select multiple adjacent cells | Click to select a cell, then hold the `shift` key and click the last cell in the range of cells that you want to select. |
| Select and edit multiple fields at the same time | Click and drag your cursor across multiple cells. This works for typing text and numbers, clicking checkboxes, and using drop-down menus in the selected cells. |
| Apply the value of a cell to the cells below or above it | Click and drag the cell's fill handle across the cells below or above. |
| Adjust the width of a column | Click the divider to the right of a column title and drag your cursor to adjust the width of the column. |

Keyboard shortcuts that you can use to help you navigate and edit properties in the Shopify bulk editor.

## Update the invalid values, then save again error message

If you receive the error message "Update the invalid values, then save again" when attempting to save your bulk edits, then one or more products or variants have invalid values that are blocking the save operation. This can occur even when the error is in a column that isn't currently displayed in your bulk editor view.

This error typically occurs when:

- A variant is missing a required SKU.
- There are metafield validation errors. If you have a high volume of metafield definitions, then it might be more efficient to [fix metafield validation errors](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/custom-data/metafields/fixing-metafield-validation-errors) first in the metafield bulk editor, and then return to bulk editing your products or variants.

To identify and resolve the invalid values, add the SKU and metafield columns in the bulk editor, and then review the values.

## Variants aren't grouped together in inventory bulk editor

When using the bulk editor for inventory, variants might not be grouped together as expected. The bulk editor displays variants in the order they were sorted before you accessed the bulk editor, not by product grouping.

The inventory bulk editor prioritizes the sorting order over product parent grouping. By default, the inventory page sorts products and variants by quantity based on stock levels at the inventory location. Because inventory is tracked at the variant level, variants from the same product might appear separated when they have different inventory quantities.

If you want variants to appear in a specific order, then sort your inventory list on the Inventory page before accessing the bulk editor.

web.title: How to Bulk Edit Products in Shopify
web.description:
I'll show you exactly how to bulk edit products in Shopify - turning those hours into minutes.

This guide walks you through three methods to bulk edit products in Shopify.

## Method 1: Using Shopify's native bulk editor
Shopify's native bulk editor works great for quick changes to a handful of products.

It loads right in your admin panel, so there's no switching between apps or learning new interfaces.
web.markdown:
![Illustrated graphic of a person bulk editing product prices in a Shopify-style spreadsheet with a shopping bag nearby](https://barn2.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/How-to-bulk-edit-products-in-Shopify-crop-820x369.png)

If you've ever spent hours clicking through products to update prices for a flash sale, you know the pain of manual editing in Shopify. I'll show you exactly how to bulk edit products in Shopify - turning those hours into minutes.

Managing a large Shopify catalog can feel like pushing a boulder uphill. You need to update hundreds of products for tomorrow's sale, fix inventory after a stocktake, or adjust prices after a supplier change. Making these changes one by one isn't just slow - it's a recipe for mistakes that can cost you sales and customer trust.

The good news is that bulk editing transforms this tedious process. Instead of spending your Saturday clicking through products, you can make sweeping changes in minutes. This means more time for strategy, marketing, and actually growing your business.

This guide walks you through three methods to bulk edit products in Shopify. I'll start with the built-in tools for quick fixes, then move to more powerful solutions like [Setary](https://apps.shopify.com/setary?utm_source=setary&utm_medium=barn2-website&utm_campaign=barn2-blog&utm_content=bulk-edit-products-shopify) that turn catalog management into a breeze.

![Setary product editor showing a grid of WooCommerce products with inline editing and column filter options](https://barn2.com/wp-content/uploads/edd/2025/06/Setary-CTA-Image-update-820x576.png)

## Method 1: Using Shopify's native bulk editor

Shopify's native bulk editor works great for quick changes to a handful of products. If you're updating prices for 20 items or adding tags to a specific collection, this free tool gets the job done without any setup.

I use the native editor when I need to make simple changes fast. It loads right in your admin panel, so there's no switching between apps or learning new interfaces. The spreadsheet view feels familiar if you've used [Excel](https://barn2.com/blog/shopify-to-excel/?utm_source=barn2&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=text&utm_content=bulk-edit-products-shopify) or [Google Sheets](https://barn2.com/blog/shopify-to-google-sheets/?utm_source=barn2&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=text&utm_content=bulk-edit-products-shopify).

The best part about the native editor is its availability. Every [Shopify plan](https://barn2.com/blog/shopify-starter-plan-review/?utm_source=barn2&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=text&utm_content=bulk-edit-products-shopify) includes it, from Basic to Plus. For stores just starting out or those with smaller catalogs, it's often all you need.

### How to bulk edit products in Shopify's admin

Shopify's [native bulk editor](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-admin/productivity-tools/bulk-editing) lets you modify multiple products simultaneously:

1. Start by navigating to your Products page in the Shopify admin. Select the products you want to edit using the checkboxes. You can choose specific items or use filters to select products by collection, vendor, or product type.
2. Once you've selected your products, click the 'Bulk edit' button at the top of the page.



![Shopify Products admin page with products selected and Bulk edit button shown for bulk product editing](https://barn2.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Shopify-default-native-bulk-editor-Products-page-820x409.jpg)

3. This opens a spreadsheet-like interface where you can see all selected products in rows. Click the 'Columns' button to add or remove fields you want to edit. Common fields include price, SKU, [inventory quantity](https://barn2.com/blog/bulk-edit-inventory-shopify/?utm_source=barn2&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=text&utm_content=bulk-edit-products-shopify), [tags](https://barn2.com/blog/shopify-bulk-edit-tags/?utm_source=barn2&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=text&utm_content=bulk-edit-products-shopify), and SEO settings.



![Shopify native bulk editor with product title, status, category, and price columns visible for bulk product editing](https://barn2.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Shopify-default-native-bulk-editor-820x150.jpg)

4. Click any cell to start editing. You can type directly into cells, copy and paste values, or drag the corner of a cell to apply the same value to multiple products. The interface supports standard keyboard shortcuts like Tab to move between cells and Ctrl+Z to undo changes.
5. After making your changes, click 'Save' to apply them to your live store. The native [Shopify bulk editor](https://setary.com/blog/bulk-edit-products-shopify/) shows a progress bar while saving, and you'll see a confirmation once complete.

### Pros and cons of Shopify's bulk editor

Advantages:

- Free and built into every Shopify plan.
- No learning curve if you've used spreadsheets before.
- Changes apply instantly to your live store.
- Works well for [editing prices](https://barn2.com/blog/bulk-edit-prices-shopify/?utm_source=barn2&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=text&utm_content=bulk-edit-products-shopify), tags, and basic product information.

Disadvantages:

- Limited to 50 products per page - frustrating for larger updates.
- Can't edit variant details in the same view as products.
- No undo button - mistakes go straight to your live store.
- Browser can freeze with large product selections.
- Missing advanced features like percentage-based price changes.

The native Shopify bulk editor hits a wall when you're managing hundreds of products. If you've got 500 items to update, that's 10 separate bulk editing sessions. Each session means new filters, new selections, and new chances for errors.

Performance issues plague larger stores. I've watched the editor struggle with just 100 products selected. The browser slows to a crawl, cells take seconds to respond to clicks, and sometimes the whole page crashes. You lose all unsaved work and have to start over. This gets worse if you're editing multiple columns or working with products that have many variants.

Luckily, there are several better ways to bulk edit Shopify products. I'll tell you about them next.

## Method 2: Using CSV files for bulk edits

[CSV files](https://flatfile.com/blog/what-is-a-csv-file-guide-to-uses-and-benefits/) offer an alternative way to bulk edit Shopify products. As Shopify explain [in their documentation](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/import-export/using-csv), CSV's can be helpful when facing major catalog overhauls. Maybe you're migrating from another platform, applying complex pricing formulas, or updating product data from your supplier's spreadsheet. CSV files handle these scenarios where the native bulk editor falls short.

The way it works is that first you [export your Shopify product](https://barn2.com/blog/shopify-export-products/?utm_source=barn2&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=text&utm_content=bulk-edit-products-shopify) s to a CSV file. You can then open it using any spreadsheet software, make the bulk editors, and re-import the products to Shopify.

This method is incredibly flexible. However, it is quite time-consuming and fiddly compared to using a proper [Shopify bulk edit app like Setary](https://apps.shopify.com/setary?utm_source=setary&utm_medium=barn2-website&utm_campaign=barn2-blog&utm_content=bulk-edit-products-shopify) (which we'll discuss in a minute).

### How to bulk edit Shopify products using CSV files

![Shopify Export products dialog showing how to download a CSV file for bulk editing products](https://barn2.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/How-to-export-Shopify-products-to-CSV-820x477.jpg)

Start by exporting your products from the Products page in Shopify:

1. Go to the 'Products' page.
2. Click 'Export'.
3. Choose which products to include - either all products or a filtered selection.
4. Select 'Plain CSV file' format and click 'Export products'.
5. Shopify will email you the file when it's ready. Open the CSV in your preferred spreadsheet program. Excel, Google Sheets, and Numbers all work fine. The file contains columns for every product field - Title, Handle, SKU, Price, Inventory, and dozens more. Each row represents either a product or a variant.
6. Make your edits carefully. The 'Handle' column is critical - it's how Shopify identifies which product to update. Never change handles unless you're creating new products. For variants, the Handle links them to their parent product. Pay attention to formatting, especially for prices (no currency symbols) and inventory (whole numbers only).
7. Save (or export) your edited file in CSV format.
8. Return to your Products page in Shopify and click 'Import'.
9. Upload your file and check 'Overwrite any current products that have the same handle'. This ensures your changes replace existing data rather than creating duplicates. Click 'Upload and continue' to start the import.

![Shopify Import products by CSV dialog for uploading a bulk-edited CSV to update existing products](https://barn2.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Import-products-to-Shopify-from-CSV-820x474.jpg)

### Pros and cons of bulk editing with CSV files

# Best Methods for Bulk Editing Shopify Products

Managing hundreds of Shopify products manually is time-consuming and creates costly errors. I’ve met merchants who have spent entire weekends clicking through product pages to update prices for flash sales or adjust inventory after stock takes. Manual editing isn’t just slow – it’s dangerous. After all, one misplaced decimal can list a $50 item for $5.

The solution is bulk editing. Instead of individual product updates, you can modify hundreds of items in minutes. It transforms catalog management from a dreaded chore into a quick task.

This guide covers three proven methods to bulk edit products Shopify stores use successfully: native tools, CSV imports, and specialized apps like [Setary](https://apps.shopify.com/setary?utm_source=setary&utm_medium=setary-website&utm_campaign=setary-blog&utm_content=bulk-edit-products-shopify). You’ll learn exactly which method fits your workflow and catalog size.

![Filter by attribute and bulk edit stock in spreadsheet WooCommerce](https://setary.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/Setary-filter-by-attribute-and-change-stock-in-bulk-edit-1024x587.jpg)The Setary spreadsheet editor provides a fast bulk edit experience

## Why Bulk Editing Matters for Shopify Stores

Bulk editing involves updating multiple products simultaneously rather than one by one. This capability separates efficient stores from those stuck in manual workflows.

Updating prices for 100 products manually takes about two hours, depending on how fast you work! With bulk editing, the same task takes five minutes. That’s 95% time savings you can redirect toward marketing or business development.

Error reduction provides another benefit. It’s inevitable that manual editing introduces typos and wrong decimal places. Bulk editing applies changes systematically, reducing errors.

There are lots of reasons to add a Shopify bulk edit tool to your store. For example:

- Flash sales require updating hundreds of products with sale prices.
- [Inventory updates](https://setary.com/blog/bulk-edit-inventory-shopify/) need quantity adjustments for every SKU.
- SEO optimization involves [adding meta descriptions at scale](https://setary.com/blog/bulk-edit-description-shopify/).
- New product lines and variants need adding to Shopify quickly and efficiently.
- Multi-location inventory requires setting accurate stock levels across warehouses.

## Method 1: Shopify’s Native Bulk Editor

### What It Is and When to Use It

Shopify’s [native bulk editor](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-admin/productivity-tools/bulk-editing) is a built-in feature that modifies multiple products through a basic spreadsheet interface. Every Shopify plan includes this tool at no extra cost.

The native editor works best for updates affecting fewer than 50 products. It lets you handle quick changes without additional apps or setup. The interface loads in your Shopify admin panel with a familiar grid layout.

### Step-by-Step: How to Bulk Edit Products Shopify Native Tool

Shopify’s native bulk editor follows a straightforward workflow:

1. First, navigate to your Products page in the Shopify admin. This displays your full product catalog with filtering options at the top.
2. Select products using checkboxes next to each item you want to edit. You can select products manually or use filters to narrow the list first. Filters help when [editing specific collections](https://setary.com/blog/bulk-edit-collections-shopify/), vendors, or product types.
3. Click the ‘Bulk edit’ button that appears at the top of the page after selecting products. This opens the bulk editing interface with your selected items.

![Shopify native bulk editor products](https://setary.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Shopify-native-bulk-editor-products-1024x510.webp)

#### Bulk edit actions

Once you’re in, you can customize columns by clicking the ‘Columns’ button. Select which product fields you want to edit – price, compare-at price, SKU, inventory quantity, tags, vendor, or SEO settings. Only enabled columns appear in the editing grid.

You can make inline edits directly in cells by clicking and typing. The interface supports familiar spreadsheet shortcuts. For example, press Tab to move between cells, use Ctrl+Z to undo changes, or drag the corner of a cell to fill values down to other products.

![Shopify native bulk editing](https://setary.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Shopify-native-bulk-editing-1024x187.webp)

Apply changes across multiple products by selecting cells and pasting values, or dragging fill handles to copy data. This works well for applying the same tag to all selected products or setting identical compare-at prices.

Save changes when you finish editing. To do this, click the ‘Save’ button to apply modifications to your live store. A progress indicator shows while Shopify processes your updates.

Remember that the native Shopify bulk editor shows only 50 products per page. If you selected more than 50 items, you’ll need to save the first page, then navigate to the next page to continue editing. This pagination creates extra steps for larger updates.

### Advantages of Native Bulk Editing

The native Shopify bulk edit tool offers several benefits that make it the right choice for certain scenarios:

- **Free on all Shopify plans** means every merchant can access [bulk editing](https://barn2.com/blog/bulk-edit-products-shopify/) without additional subscription costs. Whether you run a Basic plan or Shopify Plus, the feature works identically.
- **No learning curve for spreadsheet users** since the interface mimics Excel and Google Sheets. Your team already knows how to navigate grids, edit cells, and use keyboard shortcuts. Training time is minimal or nonexistent.
- **Instant changes to your live store** happen when you click Save. There’s no export-import cycle or processing delay. Updates appear on your storefront immediately, which works well for time-sensitive changes.
- **It works well for prices, tags, and basic fields** that don’t require complex transformations or formulas. Simple updates like changing all prices in a collection or adding a seasonal tag happen quickly.

### Limitations You Should Know

The native Shopify bulk editor has several constraints that make it unsuitable for larger operations or frequent updates:

- Its **50-product limit per page** creates tedious workflows when updating hundreds of items. You’ll edit 50 products, save, navigate to the next page, and repeat. A 500-product update requires 10 separate editing sessions.
- **You cannot edit variant details** in the same view as parent products. Variants require separate bulk editing sessions, making products with multiple size or color options harder to manage comprehensively.
- **No undo button** means that changes apply immediately and permanently to your live store. A mistaken edit goes live instantly. You’ll need to manually revert errors or restore from backups. I find this particularly nerve-wracking when making price changes.
- **Browser performance issues** with large selections slow everything down. Even with just 100 products selected, I’ve experienced sluggish cell responses and occasional browser freezes. The interface simply wasn’t designed for processing large datasets.
- **Missing advanced features** like percentage-based price changes, find-and-replace operations, or formula support. You can’t tell the native editor to “increase all prices by 15%” – you’d need to calculate new prices externally, then paste them in.

These limitations push many Shopify merchants toward alternative methods when their stores grow beyond simple bulk editing needs. I’ll tell you about these next. First, we’ll look at the fiddly but free CSV method; then we’ll look at some easy-to-use, fully-featured Shopify bulk edit apps like [Setary](https://apps.shopify.com/setary?utm_source=setary&utm_medium=setary-website&utm_campaign=setary-blog&utm_content=bulk-edit-products-shopify).

## Method 2: Bulk Editing with CSV Files

### When CSV Imports Make Sense

CSV files are comma-separated value spreadsheets that store data in plain text. Shopify lets you [export product data to CSV files](https://setary.com/blog/shopify-export-products/) for editing in spreadsheet software, then import them back.

This method suits specific scenarios, such as one-time massive catalog overhauls, platform migrations, and supplier data integration. CSV files provide flexibility for complex changes requiring formulas, as you get the full capabilities of spreadsheet software like Excel, Mac Numbers, or Google Sheets.

### Complete CSV Bulk Edit Workflow

The CSV process involves three distinct phases: export, edit, and import. You need to go through each of these every time you want to bulk edit product data in Shopify. (If that’s too much of a pain, then skip to Method 3 which is much quicker!)

#### Step 1 – Export Products:

![Export Shopify to CSV](https://setary.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Export-Shopify-to-CSV-1024x595.jpg)

1. Go to your Products page in Shopify admin and click the ‘Export’ button in the upper right.
2. Choose which products to include – all products, products from a specific collection, or products matching current filter criteria. This selection determines what appears in your CSV file.
3. Select ‘Plain CSV file’ format from the export options. This creates a standard CSV compatible with all spreadsheet programs.
4. Click ‘Export products’ to generate the file. Shopify processes the export and emails you a download link. Large catalogs may take several minutes to process.

#### Step 2 – Edit the Spreadsheet:

1. Open the CSV file once it’s downloaded. Use Excel, [Google Sheets](https://setary.com/blog/shopify-to-google-sheets/), Numbers, or any spreadsheet program. The file contains columns for every product field Shopify tracks.
2. Key columns you’ll see include Handle (unique product identifier), Title, Body HTML (description), Vendor, Type, [Product Tags](https://setary.com/blog/shopify-bulk-edit-tags/), Published, Price, Compare At Price, SKU, Barcode, Inventory Quantity, and many more. Each row represents either a product or a variant.
3. The Handle column is critical. This unique identifier tells Shopify which product to update during import. Never change Handle values unless you’re creating new products. Modifying handles creates duplicates instead of updating existing items.
4. Make your edits carefully. Remove currency symbols from prices (write 29.99 not $29.99). Use whole numbers for inventory quantities. Maintain consistent formatting across all entries. Empty cells may clear existing data during import depending on your import settings.

Pay special attention to variant relationships. Shopify products with multiple variants appear across multiple rows. All rows sharing the same Handle belong to one product. The first row contains product-level data, while subsequent rows contain variant-specific information.

Save your edited file in CSV format. Some spreadsheet programs ask you to confirm the CSV format and warn about lost formatting. Confirm the save – Shopify only needs the plain text data.

#### **Step 3 – Import the Updated Spreadsheet:**

![Shopify CSV import](https://setary.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Shopify-CSV-import-1024x592.jpg)

1. Return to your Products page in the Shopify admin and click ‘Import’ in the top right.
2. Upload your edited CSV file using the file selector. Shopify validates the file structure before proceeding.
3. Check the ‘Overwrite any current products that have the same handle’ option. This crucial setting tells Shopify to update existing products rather than creating duplicates. Without this checkbox, Shopify treats every row as a new product.
4. Click ‘Upload and continue’ to start processing. Shopify shows a summary of changes it will make – products to create, products to update, and any errors detected in your file.
5. Review this summary carefully. It’s your last chance to catch mistakes before changes go live. If something looks wrong, cancel the import and fix your CSV file.
6. Confirm the import to proceed. Shopify processes changes in the background and emails you when complete. Large imports may take 10-15 minutes depending on catalog size and Shopify’s current server load.

### CSV Method Benefits

[CSV imports](https://setary.com/blog/shopify-csv-import/) provide plenty of capabilities that Shopify’s native bulk editor cannot match. They let you:

- **Edit unlimited products** in one import without pagination limits. Update 5,000 products as easily as 50 products. The only constraint is file size, which rarely matters for product data.
- **Work offline in familiar tools** using the spreadsheet software you already know. No internet connection required while editing. Make changes during downtime, then upload when ready.
- **Apply complex spreadsheet formulas** to calculate new prices, generate SKUs algorithmically, or manipulate text fields. If you can build it in Excel, you can apply it to your Shopify products.
- **Create complete catalog backups** as a byproduct of the export process. I keep timestamped CSV exports before major changes, creating a safety net for recovery if needed.
- **Edit any field** including [metafields](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/custom-data/metafields/bulk-edit-metafields) and advanced product data – far more than you can in the native bulk editor. The CSV contains every piece of information Shopify stores about your products. You can bulk edit fields that don’t even appear in the native bulk editor.

### Major CSV Risks and Drawbacks

The flexibility of CSV editing comes with significant dangers:

- **High error risk** causes imports to fail or corrupt data. One misplaced comma breaks CSV parsing.
- **No validation** means you won’t know about problems until after import completes.
- **Cannot undo imports** once they finish. You need a backup CSV to reverse changes.
- **The time-consuming 3-step cycle** adds friction with export-edit-import workflows.
- **Complex for non-technical users** who lack spreadsheet experience.

### Why Experienced Merchants Avoid CSV

Most Shopify merchants have a CSV horror story. They’ll use it once for migration, then look for better tools. The lack of preview and undo makes CSV editing too risky for regular use. So with that in mind, let’s move on to Method 3 – the best way to bulk edit products in Shopify.

## Best Practices for Safe Bulk Editing

**1\. Always Create Backups First**

Export product data before major changes. Save CSV files with timestamps like “products-backup-2025-11-13.csv”. Keep the last three backups for multiple recovery points.

**2\. Test with Small Batches First**

Edit 5-10 products before editing 500. Check your storefront after the test to verify changes display correctly. This catches problems when they’re easy to fix.

**3\. Use Filters Carefully**

Double-check filter criteria before applying changes. Review the product list to verify you’ve selected exactly what you intended. Apps with preview features provide extra safety.

**4\. Understand Variant Relationships**

Know how variant changes affect parent products. Be careful with SKU changes since they may break integrations. Use apps that clearly show variant hierarchy.
